title: The Water Cycle
seo_title: Year 4 Science: The Water Cycle Worksheets (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Identify sources of water and describe key processes in the water cycle, including movement of water through the environment and its use as a resource (summary of the Australian Curriculum v9.0 Science content description).
meta_desc: Free Year 4 science worksheets on the water cycle: evaporation, condensation, precipitation and collection, plus rainwater tanks, dams and saving water in Australia. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: The Sun drives the water cycle, and the same water is used again and again.
body_html:
How to think about it

The water cycle moves the same water around again and again.

  • Evaporation: the Sun heats water and it becomes water vapour (a gas). Plants also give off water vapour (transpiration).
  • Condensation: water vapour cools and forms tiny droplets: clouds, fog and dew.
  • Precipitation: rain, hail or snow falls. Collection: water gathers in rivers, dams, oceans and under the ground.
Example

Dew on the grass at dawn. Which process?

cool night air

water vapour turns to liquid

Answer: condensation

Example

A puddle dries up. Where did the water go?

it evaporated

it is water vapour in the air

Answer: into the air

Common mistakes

  • Thinking clouds are water vapour (they are tiny water droplets).
  • Thinking water disappears when it evaporates.
  • Mixing up evaporation (liquid to gas) and condensation (gas to liquid).

faq.q: What are the four main stages of the water cycle?
Why is water important to save in Australia?
faq.a: Australia is the driest inhabited continent. Rainfall changes a lot from year to year, so droughts are common.

faq.q: Where does the water in a cloud come from?
faq.a: It comes from water that evaporated from oceans, lakes, rivers, soil and plants, then cooled and condensed into droplets.

items.q: Why is the water cycle called a cycle?
c: It moves in a straight line.
The same water moves around again and again.
items.e: Water is never used up.

items.q: In the water cycle, what comes after condensation?
items.e: The cycle repeats again and again.

items.q: What happens during condensation in the water cycle?
c: Water vapour rises, cools and turns into tiny droplets that form clouds.
Water runs into rivers, lakes, the sea and underground, and collects there.
The Sun warms water in seas, lakes and puddles, and it turns into water vapour.
Droplets join together and fall as rain, sleet, snow or hail.
items.e: Evaporation → condensation → precipitation → collection.
